tweets: A callee can reenter a contract before its first invocation finishes.
This happens when state is updated after an external call, allowing repeated use of stale state.
The root cause is that control flow passes to the callee before the initial update completes.
Remediation involves performing internal state changes before the external call.
Using checks-effects-interactions ensures state is safe before any interaction occurs.
A reentrancy lock blocks the unwanted callback into the protected path.
It does not prevent control passing to the external callee itself.
